title: Real-Time EEG-Guided HD-tDCS to Suppress Epileptic Spikes
official: A Real-Time Electroencephalography-Guided Non-Invasive Brain Stimulation to Suppress Epileptic Seizures
summary: This study tests whether high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation (HD-tDCS), delivered when epileptic spikes are detected on EEG during sleep, reduces spike rates in adults with focal epilepsy, and which current flow direction (outward, left, right, anterior or posterior) is most effective. Participants stay overnight up to 10 times over 3 months and receive active or sham stimulation, assigned at random for each stimulation run.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Focal epilepsy
* Documented epileptic spikes on prior EEG recording
* Steady doses of outpatient antiseizure medications for the preceding 8 weeks

Exclusion Criteria:

* Age under 18 years
* Inability to provide direct informed consent (e.g., developmental delay, cognitive impairment)
* Contraindications to scalp EEG (e.g., lice, scabies, other skin infection, scalp psoriasis, hypersensitivity, other severe dermatological condition)
* Implanted stimulatory devices (e.g., vagus nerve stimulator, cardiac pacemaker)
* History of stroke, brain surgery or traumatic brain injury
* Metal implant
* Pregnancy
